The light blue of the selected-row highlight is close to the 'recommended allocation' colour. Numbers can only be found by hovering, one supply at a time. At the current budget (5,837,591, α 0.20) Cox's Bazar gets: antimalarials 285 (demand 363, stock 78, unmet 0); ORS 5,610 (demand 9,330, stock 1,850, unmet 1,870); IV saline 385 (demand 1,408, stock 638, unmet 385); beds 0 (demand 42, stock 443); NS1 kits 0 (demand 131, stock 486). tasks.stuck: The text file is a broken extraction of a two-column page. The reference list comes first, sentences are interleaved with citations ('budget between districts. It also gives each division a / [1] World Health Organization...'), page footers sit mid-text, and template placeholders remain ('TEAMMATE: ... Half a page in your own words.'). After digging I found the three recommendations: (1) act on the weekly warning list, check every warning, and expect about 2 false alarms a year per district; (2) send supplies by measured shortfall, not population (68% vs 34% of shortfall covered at half the money), where the equity floor is a policy choice; (3) prepare before each season, with the only worked example being Dhaka dengue: supplies by mid-July, campaign in late June. What it asks of me: investigate every warning and plan stock on the high end of the range. It is written to the Director, and no Cox's Bazar or Chattogram dates are given. It says 'click a district to see its weekly cases', which does not apply in my district view. It says 'a triangle marks a warning', but the triangles are past alerts. Its 68%/34% figures do not match anything I saw on the dashboard (at the lowest budget the summary said '50% of shortfall covered').
quotes: Why does it start with references? Where is the first page?
It tells Dhaka when to stock up. When do I stock up for malaria in Cox's Bazar?
'Half a page in your own words' — this is not finished.

issues.problem: No 'alert this week' indicator. 'Alert wks' counts alerts across the 26-week range (mine are from Aug-Sep), so an orange badge at #1 reads as a current alert.
issues.suggested_fix: Add a status line for the user's district: 'This week: no alert / ALERT for <disease>', and rename the column 'Alerts in last 26 weeks'.

issues.problem: Shows '<5' for the district and for every division (Dhaka division dengue mean 85.68/100k) because the last week (29 Dec) is partial (data through 31 Dec). It reads as 'almost no cases'.
issues.suggested_fix: Use the last complete week, or mark it 'incomplete week'; show its date in the header.

issues.problem: In district view the rank compares one district with eight divisions, which are not evaluated (0 / 0.00 shown as if measured). Cox's Bazar is '#1' even for diarrhoea with 0 alerts.
issues.suggested_fix: Show '–' for unevaluated division rows, and rank the district against the districts of its division or nationally (as a percentile) without showing their identities.
